bib.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Compression Algorithms for Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list (from about char 105309) skimmed for lineage only.

question: How can language models be compressed without sacrificing accuracy, and what are the trends, fundamentals and open problems across compression algorithm families (including low-cost ones usable on LLMs)?
contributions: Overview: summarise the trend of compression algorithms for language models, covering both high-cost and low-cost algorithms.
Analysis: select three representative algorithms each from pruning, quantization and other compression, and elaborate their details.
Discussion: discuss compression algorithms and introduce promising future research topics.

results.claim: Structured pruning (ZipLM) reaches up to 15x BERT inference speedup with small accuracy loss; pruning gives the highest acceleration among compression families.
results.setup: BERT-base, MNLI/QQP/SQuAD1.1, high-cost structured pruning (neurons, heads, sublayers) on target hardware
results.quote: up to 15 times with a small accuracy degradation

results.claim: Low-cost pruning is far cheaper than high-cost: Kprune prunes BERT in 10 minutes on MNLI versus up to 40 hours for high-cost methods.
results.setup: BERT on MNLI; high-cost ~400K training examples vs low-cost ~2K calibration examples (Fig 6)
results.quote: prunes BERT within 10 minutes on the MNLI

results.claim: SparseGPT prunes a 175B-parameter LLM in about three hours on one A100 GPU.
results.setup: Unstructured / 2:4 one-shot pruning with calibration data
results.quote: SparseGPT achieves remarkable efficiency that prunes 175B

results.claim: SparseGPT 2:4 on OPT-175B: perplexity 8.35 to 8.74 at 50% compression, 1.66x speedup.
results.setup: WikiText2 perplexity, OPT-175B, 2:4 sparsity, low-cost; speedup is geometric mean over individual affine transformations
results.table: Table 3, row SparseGPT [40] OPT-175B 2:4, columns Perplexity PLM/Comp. and Speedup

results.claim: At 70% sparsity on LLaMA-7B (WikiText2), Wanda reaches perplexity 85.77 against 26.30 for SparseGPT, showing the weakness of weight-update-free pruning at high sparsity.

results.table: Table 3, rows Wanda and SparseGPT, LLaMA-7B, column Perplexity Comp.

results.claim: RPTQ degrades when activations are quantized below 8 bits.
Memory overhead, not compute, dominates LLM inference time, so recent LLM quantization focuses on weight-only methods that cut weight-loading latency but need dequantization.
Pruning decoder-only models is harder than encoder-only: structured pruning of GPT-2 degrades below 50% compression while BERT survives 75%.
About 40% of attention heads are prunable with negligible accuracy loss.
results.quote: approximately 40% of attention heads are prunable with negligible accuracy degradation

results.claim: LoRA cuts fine-tuning memory for GPT-3 175B from 1.2TB to 350GB.
Low-rank approximation reaches the highest parameter compression, up to 50 times, but only in high-cost scenarios.
results.quote: up to 50 times, in high-cost compression scenarios

results.claim: NAS-BERT needs three days on 32 P40 GPUs to search for BERT-base (110M params), so NAS does not extend to LLMs.
results.quote: NAS-BERT [158] requires three days with 32 P40 GPUs

results.claim: Authors' two desired properties for low-cost compression: optimise the task objective directly instead of layer-wise reconstruction error, and compress gradually and iteratively.

limits: A survey: no new experiments. All numbers in Tables 2-7 are collected from the cited papers, under differing models, calibration sets and hardware, so cross-row comparison is loose; speedups are not measured under a common setup.
Compression rate is memory reduction, or FLOPs reduction where memory is not reported (marked with a spade symbol); the two are not comparable.
Knowledge distillation and low-rank tables cover encoder-only (BERT-scale) models only, because decoder-only studies are lacking.

Coverage ends in early 2024 (arXiv v1, Jan 2024). It does not cover KV-cache compression, speculative decoding, FP8/FP4 formats or serving-level adaptivity; later quantization and sparsity work has dated the LLM tables.
Authors concede low-cost algorithms suffer severe accuracy degradation and structured LLM pruning has much room for improvement.
practices: Use low-cost (calibration-data, post-training) compression for LLMs; use high-cost retraining only for small models like BERT (Sec 2.3, 3.3, 4.3).
Prefer weight-only quantization for LLMs because memory loading dominates inference time (Sec 4.3.2).
Use scale (symmetric) quantization when compute cost matters and affine quantization for skewed distributions (Sec 4.2.1).
Calibrate clipping range with percentile or KL-divergence rather than min/max when outliers exist (Sec 4.2.1).
Treat activation outliers specially (keep related weights in full precision as OWQ, or cluster and reorder as RPTQ) (Sec 4.4).
For structured pruning, prune large granularities (sublayers, layers) to actually gain GPU speedup; head or neuron pruning rarely removes whole matmuls (Sec 3.2).
Use semi-structured 2:4 sparsity when speedup on NVIDIA A100 is needed (Sec 3.2, 3.4).
Compress iteratively with mild steps plus error compensation rather than one shot (Sec 6.2).
Optimise a task-specific objective, not only sublayer reconstruction error (Sec 6.2).
Use LoRA-style PEFT to compensate compression error cheaply (Sec 5.5, 6.1).
Combine compression families (e.g. pruning plus quantization) for higher rates; few works unify three or more (Sec 6.1).

terms.definition: Given an accurate large PLM T and dataset D, generate a tiny but still accurate compressed model S that meets cost constraints in FLOPs, memory or latency.
Algorithms that require extensive retraining processes on large datasets; more accurate but intractable for LLMs.
Algorithms that perform only a simple weight-tuning process on small calibration data; applicable to LLMs but with severe accuracy degradation.

terms.term: mask search problem / error compensation problem
terms.definition: The two pruning sub-problems: choosing components to prune, and reducing the pruning error.
Semi-structured pruning pattern with 2 zeros in 4 consecutive elements, accelerated on NVIDIA A100.
Mapping continuous real values to their nearest integers; simple but often severely degrades performance.
Training-free quantization of a pretrained model without retraining or fine-tuning after quantization.
Apply quantization to a pretrained model, then retrain or fine-tune to recover; uses STE for the non-differentiable rounding.
Quantize only weights while keeping activations full precision; reduces memory loading but needs dequantization.
Dynamic computes activation clipping ranges at inference (better accuracy, slower); static precomputes them from calibration data.
How sublayers of teacher and student are matched for distillation.
